_note: What applicants see when they pick a team on /join, and the questions that team asks (plus `everyone`, asked of every applicant). Full board wording, open questions and suggestions are in docs/TEAMS.md. The names must match TEAMS in src/lib/submissions.ts and fable-cms src/lib/applications.ts.

teams.name: Web Development
teams.short: Builds and runs the club's websites and apps.
teams.about: Web Development turns the club's ideas into working, deployed websites and apps, then keeps them running and secure. You don't need to write every line yourself, but you should understand how a modern stack fits together.
lookingFor: Planning and shipping sites or apps from the club's ideas
Understanding tech stacks and how the pieces connect (hosting, databases, auth, APIs)
Looking after the club's GitHub repositories
Interest in security: testing and hardening what we build
niceToHave: UI design or Figma skills, for the artwork on our sites and apps
questions: Pick a website or app you use a lot. How do you think it is put together: what runs in the browser, where the data lives, how it is hosted? Guesses are fine.
Have you built, set up or looked after a site, app or repo before, with or without AI? Tell us your part, and add a link if you have one.

teams.name: Agentic AI
teams.short: Builds AI systems that act on their own, and the automation around them.
teams.about: Agentic AI goes past prompting: we build agents and automated systems that do real work, and the pipelines that test and ship them. We want people who already use AI tools well and can show something they have made.
lookingFor: Real experience building with AI tools such as Claude Code, with work you can show
Agents with tool calling and memory, or several agents working together
Automating workflows end to end, including CI/CD and basic DevOps
Python or TypeScript fundamentals, enough to debug what the AI writes
niceToHave: RAG, vector databases or context engineering
Frameworks such as LangGraph or the Claude Agent SDK
questions: Tell us about something you have made with AI tools: what it does, which tools you used and what broke along the way. Add a link if you have one.
Pick one repetitive job in a club or at college, like reminders, approvals or attendance. How would you automate it end to end, and how would you know it is working?

teams.name: Projects
teams.short: The club's planners: ideas, research and project direction.
teams.about: Projects is where the club's ideas start. You brainstorm what we should build, check whether an idea is new and actually doable, and plan it so the other teams can deliver it.
lookingFor: Coming up with project and event ideas
Checking whether an idea is original (has it been done?) and feasible (can we build it in time?)
Turning an idea into a plan with clear steps for the other teams
Curiosity about what is new in AI
niceToHave: Experience running or planning a project, in college or outside it
questions: Pitch one project the club could build, in a few lines. Who is it for, and why hasn't it been done (or done well) already?
How would you check that idea is doable in one semester? What would you look up or try first?

teams.name: Operations
teams.short: Plans and runs events, schedules and the logistics behind them.
teams.about: Operations makes things happen on the day. You plan events and workshops, keep the teams talking to each other, and handle logistics, registrations and records so nothing falls through the cracks.
lookingFor: Planning and coordinating events, workshops and club activities
Managing timelines, schedules and who does what
Handling logistics, resources, registrations and attendance
Staying calm and solving problems when plans change
Keeping documentation, reports and records up to date
Strong organisation, communication and time management
niceToHave: Experience in event management, team coordination or running operations
questions: The speaker cancels two hours before an event. Walk us through what you do next.
Tell us about an event, fest or team activity you helped run. What was your part?

teams.name: Finance
teams.short: Sponsors, budgets and the money side of events.
teams.about: Finance keeps the club funded and its events paid for. You reach out to sponsors, track what we spend, and sort out the practical costs of events like food and materials.
lookingFor: Reaching out to and talking with sponsors
Budgeting and tracking costs
Event logistics that cost money, such as food and materials
Handling event registrations with the Operations team
Being careful and reliable with numbers
questions: Pitch the club to a sponsor in three or four sentences. What do they get back?
A workshop for 60 people has ₹5,000. Roughly how would you split it, and what would you cut first if it dropped to ₹3,000?

teams.name: Creative & Communications
teams.short: Design, posters, videos and the club's look online.
teams.about: Creative makes everything people see from the club: posters, social media posts, event content and videos. You should already have hands-on time with at least one design tool.
lookingFor: Hands-on experience with at least one design tool: Canva, Photoshop, Illustrator or Figma
Posters, social media creatives or event content
A feel for colour, typography, layout and composition
Basic photo and video editing
Willingness to pick up new tools
niceToHave: Video editing in Premiere Pro, CapCut or DaVinci Resolve
questions: Share a poster, post, video or design you made (a link is best) and tell us which tool you used.
Pick a post or page from any club or brand. What is one thing you would change about how it looks, and why?

teams.name: Not sure yet
teams.short: Pick this if you'd like us to help you choose.
teams.about: That's fine. Tell us below what you'd like to build or learn, and we'll suggest a team during the short chat.
questions: What would you like to build or learn in the club?
What are you already good at, in tech or outside it?

everyone: Tell us about something you committed to and saw through, even when it got boring or hard. What was your part, and what did it take?
